permit.exempt_list_quote: When is a Permit Not Required? Below is a list of work that does not need to be permitted. (For a full list please see ICC 2021 International Residential Code, Section R105.2, Work exempt from permit) Building: Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops, and similar finish work. Other than storm shelters, one-story detached accessory structures, provided that the floor area does not exceed 200 square feet (18.58 m2). Check with Zoning for structures under 200 sq ft. Prefabricated swimming pools that are less than 24 inches (610 mm) deep. Fences not over 7 feet high. Check with Zoning for fences under 6 ft. Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet (1219 mm) in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge. Swings and other playground equipment. Decks not exceeding 200 square feet (18.58 m2) in area, that are not more than 30 inches (762 mm) above grade at any point, are not attached to a dwelling and do not serve the exit door required by Section R311.4. [Electrical, Mechanical and Plumbing lists follow; the plumbing list covers stopping leaks, clearing stoppages and 'the removal and reinstallation of water closets, provided such repairs do not involve or require the replacement or rearrangement of valves, pipes, or fixtures.']
permit.note: The list is in the city's guide 'Your Guide to Building Permits & Inspections and the Metropolitan Planning Commission' (PDF created March 6, 2026). It points to the residential code's exempt list for the full text and does not name a commercial list; toilet partitions are not named. The Permits & Inspections page says 'Permits are not required for painting or flooring' and lists 'Residential / commercial remodel' among projects that need a permit. The city's FAQ says a permit is required to 'Construct, enlarge, alter, repair or move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a structure'. The ordinance behind these pages was not read.
permit.second_quote: Building plans must be submitted and approved for all construction and reconstruction of buildings in Shreveport. Permits are not required for painting or flooring. Permits are required for the following projects: [...] Residential / commercial remodel
permit.third_quote: A permit is required whenever an owner, authorized agent, or contractor proposes to: Construct, enlarge, alter, repair or move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a structure
permit.office: City of Shreveport Permits and Inspections Division, Government Plaza, 505 Travis Street, Suite 130

contractor.quote: City Registration. Anyone desiring to engage in any residential or commercial construction, electrical, mechanical, or plumbing activities within the jurisdiction must register with the permits and inspections division to engage in said activity. This registration requires annual renewal for all trades and the maintaining of current liability insurance.
contractor.second_quote: Any unregistered person or contractor wishing to perform air conditioning / heating, electrical, and/or plumbing within the City of Shreveport must have a contractor's registration.
contractor.third_quote: Commercial / industrial projects costing $50,000 or more must be constructed by a contractor licensed by the State of Louisiana and all insurance requirements are to be on file. Out-of-state contractors must post a bond required by the Louisiana Department of Revenue and Taxation prior to the issuance of any construction permits.
contractor.note: The two city sources differ: the registration page (the local-rules entry's source) names only air conditioning/heating, electrical and plumbing; the 2026 permit guide says anyone doing residential or commercial construction must register. The page text reports both and sends the reader to the division.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Shreveport job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Louisiana humidity and see the local rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Shreveport hospitals, casinos, schools and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Louisiana's rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and state law has every city and parish enforce them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** Louisiana has scheduled newer editions of its building and plumbing rules to take effect that day. Ask Shreveport Permits and Inspections which edition applies to your project.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Shreveport requires a permit to alter or remodel a building. Its permit guide lists finish work that needs none: painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. The list doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask Shreveport Permits and Inspections (318-673-6100) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: Shreveport's permit guide says anyone doing residential or commercial construction, electrical, mechanical or plumbing work in its jurisdiction must register with Permits and Inspections, renew each year and keep liability insurance. The city's registration page names only air conditioning and heating, electrical and plumbing contractors, so ask the division (318-673-6100) whether your installer needs to register. Louisiana requires a state commercial contractor license for commercial projects of $50,000 or more, labor and materials included, so smaller jobs fall below the state requirement. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a commercial project of $50,000 or more, the contractor needs a Louisiana state license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Louisiana has no state wage law for public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded jobs, at the rate the U.S. Department of Labor sets for the parish. For a carpenter on building work in Caddo Parish that is $17.87 an hour plus $1.67 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.6% in Shreveport: 5% state, 2.75% city, 1.5% Caddo Parish School Board and 0.35% parish law enforcement. Addresses in the city's Mall Economic Development District pay 1% more.
page.buyers_extra: - **Casinos and hotels:** finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms, HDPE or phenolic where crowds and nightly washdown are hard on stalls.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (ADA-ABA Accessibility Guidelines), enforced by the Louisiana Office of State Fire Marshal; Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code: International Building Code, 2021 Edition, with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.103) and International Plumbing Code, 2021 Edition, with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.111), in force since January 1, 2023, with the 2024 editions scheduled for January 1, 2027, enforced in Shreveport by the Division of Permits and Inspections; 2021 International Residential Code, Section R105.2 (work exempt from permit, as cited in the city's permit guide); NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code.
